blended family = a family in which parents and children from previous relationships live together
next of kin = the person legally recognised as your closest family member
sibling rivalry = competition or jealousy between brothers and sisters
nuclear family = two parents and their children living as one household
single-parent family = a household in which one parent brings up the children
foster family = a family that cares for a child who is not legally theirs
adoptive parent = an adult who has legally become a child's parent
breadwinner = the person whose wage mainly supports the household
dependent = a person who relies on someone else for money or care
upbringing = the way a child is raised and taught at home
in-laws = the family of your husband or wife
spouse = a husband or wife
fiancé = a man who is engaged to be married
fiancée = a woman who is engaged to be married
widow = a woman whose husband has died
widower = a man whose wife has died
descendant = a person related to you who is born later, such as a grandchild
ancestor = a person in your family who lived a long time ago
offspring = a person's child or children
kinship = the state of being related by blood or marriage
family ties = the emotional and practical bonds between relatives
family reunion = a gathering of relatives who do not usually all meet
estranged = no longer in contact or on friendly terms with a relative
black sheep = the member of a family who is seen as a disappointment
close-knit = having strong, loyal relationships within a group
dysfunctional family = a family whose relationships are regularly harmful or chaotic
immediate family = your parents, children, brothers and sisters, and usually your spouse
godparent = an adult who promises to support a child, often at a christening
legal guardian = a person with the legal right to care for a child
heir = a person who will receive property when someone dies
inherit = to receive money or property from someone who has died
last will = a legal document saying who should receive your property after death
family heirloom = a valuable object passed down through generations
family background = the social and family circumstances you grow up in
family values = beliefs about how relatives should treat one another
household = the people who live together in one home, and that home as a unit
half-sibling = a brother or sister with whom you share only one parent
distant relative = a family member you are not closely related to
sandwich generation = adults who care for their children and their ageing parents at once
ageing parents = mothers and fathers who need more support as they grow old
homemaker = a person whose main work is running the home rather than paid employment
stay-at-home parent = a mother or father who looks after children instead of going out to work
family feud = a long, bitter quarrel between relatives
take after = to resemble an older relative in looks or character
look up to = to admire and respect someone
keep in touch = to continue communicating with someone
get on with = to have a friendly relationship with someone
fall out with = to stop being friendly after an argument
make up with = to become friends again after a quarrel
break up = to end a romantic relationship
split up = to end a relationship or marriage; to start living apart
go out with = to have a romantic relationship with someone
ask out = to invite someone to go on a date
on the rocks = in serious difficulty, especially a relationship
tie the knot = to get married
walk down the aisle = to go to the front of a church or venue to get married
best man = a male friend who supports the groom at a wedding
maid of honour = a female friend who supports the bride at a wedding
engagement = an agreement to get married; the period before the wedding
cohabit = to live together as a couple without being married
trial separation = a period when a couple lives apart to test whether the relationship can continue
custody = the legal right to care for a child after parents separate
child maintenance = money paid by a parent to help raise a child they do not live with
leave the nest = to move out of your parents' home and live independently
empty nest = the situation when children have moved out and parents remain at home
soulmate = a person you feel uniquely close to, often romantically
kindred spirit = a person who shares your attitudes and feelings
mutual friend = a person who is a friend of both you and someone else
fair-weather friend = someone who is kind only when life is easy
companion = a person you spend time with and who keeps you company
inner circle = the small group of people you trust most
keep himself to himself = to avoid socialising much and stay private
confide in = to tell someone private thoughts because you trust them
shoulder to cry on = a person who listens and comforts you when you are upset
make it up with = to become friends again after a quarrel
possessive = wanting to control a partner or friend and their time
supportive = giving help and encouragement in a kind way
take for granted = to fail to appreciate someone or something because they always seem available
drift apart = to become less close gradually, without a big argument
catch up with = to talk with someone you have not seen and hear their news
see eye to eye = to agree with someone; to share the same opinion
hit it off = to like someone immediately and get on well
have a lot in common = to share interests, values or experiences
patch things up = to repair a relationship after a quarrel
on speaking terms = willing to talk to someone after a disagreement
cold shoulder = unfriendly behaviour that shows you are ignoring someone
arm's length = not becoming too close or involved
platonic = close and affectionate but not romantic or sexual
commitment = the decision to stay loyal to a person or a relationship
compatibility = the ability of two people to live or work together well
unfaithful = having a romantic or sexual relationship outside your partnership
reconciliation = the process of becoming friends or partners again after a serious quarrel
wear the trousers = to be the person who makes the main decisions in a relationship
follow in their footsteps = to do the same job or live in a similar way as someone older
boomerang child = an adult who returns to live with parents after living away
striking resemblance = a very noticeable likeness between two people
chore = a regular, often boring job that must be done at home
quality time = time spent giving someone your full attention
run errands = to go out to do small practical jobs such as shopping or posting a parcel
daily grind = the tiring, repetitive routine of everyday life
hectic = full of busy, rushed activity
leisurely = done slowly, without rushing
night owl = a person who prefers to stay up late
early bird = a person who likes to get up and start early
household budget = a plan for how a household will spend its money
share the chores = to divide housework fairly among the people who live together
put things off = to delay tasks you ought to do
financially independent = able to pay for your own life without help from parents
move out = to leave your parents' home and live elsewhere
housemate = a person who shares a rented house with you
spare room = an extra bedroom used for visitors or a tenant
personal space = the physical and emotional room you need around yourself
privacy = the state of not being watched or interrupted
nosy = too interested in other people's private lives
overprotective = trying too hard to keep someone from any risk or independence
lenient = not strict; allowing more freedom than usual
rebellious = resisting rules and authority, especially as a teenager
adolescent = a young person between childhood and adulthood; typical of that age
curfew = a time by which you must be home in the evening
nag = to keep complaining or reminding someone in an annoying way
juggle = to deal with several responsibilities at the same time
settle down = to start living a calmer, more stable life, often with a partner
put down roots = to make a place your long-term home
house-proud = taking great care that your home looks clean and attractive
make ends meet = to have just enough money for basic needs
well-off = having plenty of money; comfortably rich
spoilt = allowed too much and therefore badly behaved or ungrateful
neglect = to fail to give someone or something the care they need
bonding = the process of becoming emotionally closer
strict upbringing = a childhood with many rules and little freedom
sheltered childhood = a childhood in which a person was protected from ordinary difficulties
pastime = an activity you do regularly for pleasure rather than work
unwind = to relax after stress or effort
couch potato = a person who spends too much time sitting and watching screens
take up = to start a hobby or activity
keen on = very interested in or enthusiastic about something
avid = very enthusiastic; doing something as often as possible
household chore = a regular job done to keep a home running
downtime = time when you are not working or busy and can rest
recharge = to rest so that you feel energetic again
binge-watch = to watch many episodes of a series one after another
potter about = to do small, pleasant jobs at home in a relaxed way
while away = to spend time in a pleasant, unhurried way
DIY = repairing or decorating your home yourself instead of paying a professional
fulfilment = a feeling that your life or hobbies are meaningful and satisfying
homebody = a person who prefers staying at home to going out
party animal = a person who loves going to parties and staying out late
life and soul of the party = the person who makes a social event lively and fun
wallflower = someone who stays at the edge of a party and does not join in
social butterfly = a person who moves easily from group to group and loves socialising
recluse = a person who lives a very private life and avoids other people
fit in = to be accepted because you seem similar to the others
left out = not included in a group or activity
small talk = polite, light conversation about unimportant topics
get-together = an informal meeting of friends or relatives
switch off = to stop thinking about work or worries; to turn a device off
screen time = the amount of time spent looking at phones, tablets or televisions
digital detox = a period when you avoid phones and other devices on purpose
stand up to = to refuse to accept unfair treatment or pressure
unwind after work = to relax once the working day is over
coming of age = the time when a young person is legally or socially recognised as an adult
condolences = formal expressions of sympathy after someone has died
housewarming = a party to celebrate moving into a new home
stag do = a party for a man before he gets married, usually with male friends
hen do = a party for a woman before she gets married, usually with female friends
wedding reception = the meal and party after a marriage ceremony
propose a toast = to invite guests to raise their glasses and wish someone well
bereavement = the state of having lost a close person through death
mourning = the period and customs of showing sadness after a death
milestone = an important event that marks progress in a life
rite of passage = a ceremony or experience that marks a new stage of life
christening = a Christian ceremony in which a baby is named and welcomed
mark an anniversary = to celebrate or remember a date each year
wedding vows = the promises a couple make to each other during the ceremony
registry office = a government office where civil marriages and births are recorded
civil ceremony = a legal wedding without a religious service
anniversary = a date you remember each year because something important happened then
family gathering = an occasion when relatives meet together
circle of friends = the group of people you spend time with socially
me time = time spent doing something for your own rest or hobby
